content: The Statens Serum Institut, commonly referred to as SSI, is a Danish sector research institute situated on the island of Amager in Copenhagen. Its primary mission is to combat and prevent infectious diseases, congenital disorders, and threats posed by ABC (atomic, biological, and chemical) weapons. Established in 1902 in the barracks along the Artillerivej road, the institute has since grown significantly beyond its original size. Administratively, the National Serum Institute operates under the Danish Ministry of the Interior and Health, which is overseen by Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen. Since 1998, the institute has been led by its president and CEO, Niels Strandberg Pedersen. In addition to conducting research in epidemiology and disease prevention, the institute is actively involved in the development and production of vaccines. It also plays a critical role in Denmark's ABC-preparedness operations. Beyond its work within Denmark, the Statens Serum Institut contributes to health promotion and monitoring efforts in Guinea-Bissau, a West African nation, through its collaboration with the Bandim Health Project.
